name: Lee Anderson
role: UK MP for Ashfield (Conservative 2019-2024, Reform UK from 2024); former Conservative deputy chairman and Reform chief whip
summary: A former coal miner turned populist-right MP who campaigns for sharply lower immigration, deportation of illegal arrivals, leaving or ignoring the ECHR, scrapping net zero and expanding coal, oil and gas. He favours tougher sentencing, work requirements and conduct tests for benefits and council housing, and says the state neglects working-class men.

assisted-dying.rationale: Voted against the Terminally Ill Adults (End of Life) Bill at second reading in Sept 2026 and against several amendments in June 2025.

close-ties-china.rationale: His remarks were about security, not economic ties.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: Said "of course" he wanted VAT removed from energy bills, while backing the Government's alternative support in 2022.

death-penalty.rationale: Asked by The Spectator in 2023 whether he would back the death penalty he said yes ("nobody has ever committed a crime after being executed"), and as a Reform MP he has since called for a referendum on it; reported secondhand.

decent-living-guarantee.rationale: Blamed the tax-credit system for benefit dependency, said struggling families need education and support rather than money thrown at them, and called able-bodied non-workers on benefits "shirkers".

decide-locally.rationale: Said local people should have the final say on whether fracking goes ahead and that houses in multiple occupation are a matter for local councils; these are specific cases, not a general principle.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Said in Dec 2025 that net zero targets should be scrapped, calling them "net stupid zero", and earlier said net zero would make no difference to the atmosphere.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Argued for mining British coal (2020), welcomed shale gas and opposed the fracking ban (2022), and said a sensible transition is needed rather than closing refineries (2025).

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: Said in 2026 there should be no need for a Minister for women or for men, "a Minister for people", and that the Equality Act need not exist.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Said Blair's tax credits damaged businesses and kept people on low hours and in benefit dependency, welcoming the universal credit taper as the fix.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Spoke at length in Feb 2026 on boys and men falling behind in education, work and wellbeing ("a hidden crisis in plain sight"), though he would rather have a Minister for people than one for men.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: His remarks concern knife carriers, not fixed sentences for serious repeat offenders.

national-law-over-international.rationale: He told the Commons the first Rwanda flight should have gone ahead by ignoring the ECHR and said the Strasbourg court was making a mockery of border protection; he voted for the Rwanda and Illegal Migration bills.

open-borders.rationale: He treats border control as a priority (detain, deport, offshore processing, Rwanda) and attacked Labour for wanting to bring back free movement.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: He called lawmakers out of touch, not corrupt.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: As a new MP he welcomed leaving the EU to regain control of borders, laws and fisheries and celebrated the UK making its own way; as a Reform MP he voted against a duty to negotiate a UK-EU customs union (Dec 2025).

priority-to-poor.rationale: Argued council houses should go on suitability (good conduct, work) rather than need and be a privilege, not a right, which rejects giving first priority to need.

proportional-representation.rationale: He complained that seats did not match votes but never called for proportional representation.

reduce-immigration.rationale: In 2023 he asked the Commons for a cap on migration, citing pressure on housing, GPs and schools, and in 2020 backed a points-based system after saying free movement had driven down wages and strained services.

rehabilitation.rationale: Speaks mainly of punishment, deterrence and making prisoners do paid work, while in 2020 he welcomed longer sentences as also giving time to rehabilitate serious offenders.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Called free speech the most important freedom (2021) and in 2026 attacked arrests for social media posts, though he voted for an Online Safety Bill amendment and against others; no direct statement on hate-speech laws.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Voted for the Strikes (Minimum Service Levels) Bill at third reading in Jan 2023 and against opposition amendments to it.

right-to-secede.rationale: Opposing the SNP is not a stated general position on secession.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Opposing prosecutions of veterans is a narrower case; no general position stated.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Said that if the state subsidises industry it should look at oil refineries (2025) and backed British steel and British-mined coal for infrastructure; no general statement on directing investment.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: Praised cost-of-living payments as real, targeted help for vulnerable households and said Labour wrongly thinks the only answer is to keep increasing benefits.

traditional-family.rationale: In Feb 2026 he said the benefits system no longer encourages the family unit and that fathers as role models mattered for boys.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Asked in a 2026 Universal Credit debate whether British people should be put first, and objected to social housing and hotels for illegal migrants while Britons wait; no statement on legal immigrants.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Said able-bodied people who refuse to work and live off the state are shirkers, and called going to work "the right and decent thing", without legislating a work test for benefits.

notes: Positions used are those of his 2019-2026 parliamentary record and statements; he defected from the Conservatives to Reform UK in March 2024 and his later statements are used where they differ. Themes searched in his Hansard record: economy, welfare, immigration, justice, free speech, energy, EU, Union, defence, health, gender and culture. Nothing found on religion, monarchy, abortion, drugs, guns, nuclear power, trade or foreign aid beyond what is recorded. TheyWorkForYou, a GB News column and a Chad column could not be opened.
